decision: Which English neural voice ships for read-aloud: pin Kokoro-82M and choose its English grapheme-to-phoneme step.
options: A. Kokoro-82M + eSpeak NG (GPL-3.0) as a separate worker the user downloads (allowed by 15.10(1))
B. Kokoro-82M + a TypeScript port of misaki's English dictionaries (Apache-2.0, the G2P Kokoro was trained with); a sentence with a word missing from the dictionary falls back to the system voice
C. System voices only (today)
why: B keeps acceptance 6.2 (0 GPL in the bundle, 0 network after the download) without shipping or downloading GPL code at all; misaki's dictionaries are the phoneme set Kokoro-82M was trained on, so quality matches the reference pipeline for in-dictionary words, and misaki uses eSpeak only as an optional fallback. A is permitted but puts GPL code on users' devices and needs a licence notice flow. C ships nothing. The Hebrew side is unaffected (no licensed Hebrew voice yet; Chatterbox waits for W11.H9).
sources: https://pypi.org/project/misaki/ (Apache-2.0; espeak is an optional out-of-dictionary fallback)

decision: Rate the local captioner's descriptions of the 50 images (30 Crossmodal-3600 + 20 Commons) 1–5 against the references (owner item 15.15).
options: A. Rate once the Mac's bench-models run (L8 has no entry: it belongs to `npm run models:day -- --only bench-models`) has produced Florence-2's captions
B. Replace the human rating with chrF against the references only (scripts/bench/tasks.mjs already computes it)
why: The acceptance is a human judgement (≥ 80 % rated ≥ 4/5); chrF against one reference undervalues a correct caption that words things differently, so B would change the acceptance. What is missing in code is a rating sheet: a page or CSV listing each image, its caption and the references, and a scorer that turns the 50 ratings into the share ≥ 4. That is ~1 h of cloud work, owed (not done in this lane).
changes: new: a rating-sheet generator and scorer (owed)
plan 6.6 evidence: the share of images rated ≥ 4

decision: Publish a 50-note site to a GitHub Pages repository of the owner's from the app (Publish site → GitHub Pages), then check it in a browser.
options: A. A throwaway public repo (e.g. lumen-publish-test) with Pages on the gh-pages branch, a fine-grained token limited to that repo (contents: write, pages: write)
B. Netlify (the app's other target)
why: GitHub Pages is the path the code deploys over REST without force or zip (#354), and a repo-scoped fine-grained token keeps the blast radius to one throwaway repo. The check is machine-readable: the site's index must list ≥ 50 pages and a missing path must return the 404 page.
sources: src/publish/deploy.ts (deploy over the GitHub REST API)
changes: none in the repo; plan 4.18 evidence: the site URL and the check's output

decision: Provide the real exports (W10.O9) and run `npm run import:diff` on each: the same export imported by lumen-md and by Obsidian Importer.
options: A. The owner's own Evernote (.enex), Notion (zip) and Google Keep (Takeout) exports, kept outside the repo
B. Public sample exports only (no personal data, but not the owner's real shapes)
recommendation: A, with B as the fallback for a format the owner has no account in
why: The acceptance is about real exports; import:diff prints counts only (notes, attachments, links, headings, tasks), so personal content never leaves the machine or enters the repo. 1,000 notes ≤ 60 s is timed on the desktop app.

decision: Where the PR security scanners (gitleaks, npm audit, cargo audit, semgrep) run on every PR now that GitHub Actions is retired.
options: A. A Buildkite agent on the owner's always-on host runs .buildkite/pipeline.yml's `security` step on every PR (already written and tested by securityScanners.test.ts), plus GitHub's own secret scanning and push protection in the repo settings
B. A local pre-push hook on the Mac only
C. GitHub code scanning default setup (runs on GitHub Actions infrastructure)
why: A is the only option that meets "3 checks on every PR" without Actions: the step exists, it fails when a scanner binary is missing in CI (LUMEN_CI/BUILDKITE), and the agent host is owner session 7. Secret scanning and push protection cost nothing on a public repo and need no workflow. B misses PRs from anyone else; C reintroduces Actions. The Mac entry L8-2.8-scanners proves the four scanners pass with every binary present.
changes: none in the repo; owner: start the Buildkite agent (accounts/factory step) and turn on secret scanning + push protection
ownerExpect: the accounts/factory checks pass (vm-timer, receipts-repo, first-status) and accounts/github secret-scanning passes
